clue.text: Justice created hold-up in charity

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the first word goes inside the second

parts.note: charity in the old sense of compassion or mercy
a hold-up is a robbery, so to rob

explanation.surface: A judge's ruling has sparked a scandal over a robbery at a charity.
explanation.walkthrough: Charity here is the old sense of mercy or compassion, not a fundraising body; the theft goes inside it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Probity is integrity and uprightness, the moral quality that justice in a person rests on.

clue.text: Qualify on times but keep going

parts.note: to pass an exam is to qualify
times as in multiplied by, as in three by four

explanation.surface: An athlete who makes the qualifying times but carries on running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is not about clocks: in arithmetic, three times four is three by four.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass by is to move on past something without stopping, continuing on one's way.

clue.text: Individual not working? It won't happen again

parts.note: a single individual is one
a machine switched off is not working

explanation.surface: A person taking a day off insists the absence was a single lapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off is a unique event or item, something done or made only a single time.

clue.text: Workers performing well as tellers

parts.note: a player performing well is in form
worker ants, the standard crossword workers

explanation.surface: Employees doing well in their jobs as bank cashiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Tellers look like bank cashiers, but here they are people who tell, passing on secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: Informants tell the police or authorities what they know, so they are tellers in the literal sense.

clue.text: Minor solver that is 50% out

parts.note: the setter addresses the solver as you

indicators.note: with half taken out, only the front half of the short word survives

parts.note: taken as written, before halving

explanation.surface: A young puzzler who has half the answers wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often use 'solver' for YOU, since the clue speaks to the person reading it.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young person, someone who is still a minor and not yet an adult.

clue.text: Cider's a novel form of cocktail

indicators.note: something novel is new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A barman claims that cider makes an original basis for a mixed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The sidecar is a classic mixed drink of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Unusual Cretan ship lacks a muscular sealing system

indicators.note: unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged
lacking something means it is missing, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: the letters of these words
the letter removed

explanation.surface: An odd vessel from Crete has no proper way of keeping water out.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphincter is a ring of muscle that closes an opening of the body by contracting.

clue.text: Disorder erupts as dance starts late

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so each word gives its first letter

parts.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Chaos breaks out when a dance begins behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' reads as tardy, but it is the sense used of someone who has died, as in 'the late king'.
explanation.definitionFit: Late in the sense of 'the late king' means no longer living, deceased.

clue.text: Arrived holding old study that reveals spy's secret identity

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so the outer word wraps the others

parts.note: came is a past tense of come, to arrive
O is a standard abbreviation for old
a den is a private study or workroom

explanation.surface: An agent arrives carrying an old paper that exposes a spy's cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A code name is an alias used to conceal the real identity of an agent or an operation.

clue.text: Instinctive responses touching cables

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a flex is a British word for an electric cable

explanation.surface: Jerking away by instinct after touching live wires.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a flex is the insulated cable on an electrical appliance; touching means concerning, as RE does.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflexes are involuntary automatic reactions of the body, made without conscious thought.

clue.text: Bundle ambassador into almost secure housing

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places the first inside the second
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: secure as in protected from harm
His Excellency, the formal address for an ambassador

explanation.surface: Diplomats bundle their envoy into a nearly safe house.
explanation.walkthrough: HE for His Excellency is the standard crossword ambassador; 'housing' is a noun on the surface but here just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheaf is a bundle, typically of corn stalks or papers, tied together.

clue.text: Found her a way out that's without precedent

indicators.note: finding a way out suggests escaping from the given order, so the letters break free and rearrange

parts.note: the letters of these words
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone freed a trapped woman in a rescue never seen before.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' of 'a way out' is also part of the fodder: FOUND HER plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unheard of has never happened or been known before, so has no earlier example to follow.

clue.text: Live with stroke that's happened earlier?

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
a forehand is a stroke in tennis

explanation.surface: A doctor asks whether a patient living with a stroke had one before.
explanation.walkthrough: A stroke looks medical, but it is the tennis shot played palm forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Beforehand means in advance, describing something done or taking place at a prior time.

clue.text: Reportedly vote against revealing wife's former title

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken of, so the word is taken by sound

parts.note: nay is a vote of no

explanation.surface: A vote reveals what a married woman used to be called.
explanation.definitionFit: Née, French for born, introduces a married woman's maiden surname, the name she held earlier.

clue.text: Subject I'm chattier about

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone admits there is a topic that makes them more talkative.
explanation.definitionFit: Arithmetic, working with numbers, is a school subject taught from the earliest years.

clue.text: I assure you, I don't want it

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom vouching for what one says
second meaning, read literally: remove the thing from my possession

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is usually a promise of reliability; read word by word, it is a plea to be relieved of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said to vouch for one's own word, while the literal reading asks someone to remove an object.

clue.text: I screeched aloud when examined

indicators.note: aloud says the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: the letter I sounds like eye; bawled means screeched, yelled loudly

explanation.surface: Someone yelled when being given a check-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball something is to look it over closely, to inspect it.

clue.text: Nearly throw up visiting farm building that's plastic

indicators.note: visiting means one piece goes in to stay inside another

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs on a farm
to retch is to heave as if about to vomit, which is nearly throwing up

explanation.surface: Someone feels sick on entering a smelly farm building made of plastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' is not a cutting signal here: retching is the heaving that comes just before vomiting, so the whole phrase is one synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic in its original sense means pliable and able to be shaped, so something easily pulled out of shape.

clue.text: Ideal stimulant to support mountain climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: an Alp is a mountain
a tonic is a restorative or stimulant

explanation.surface: A climber finds a pick-me-up just the thing on the way up a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To support' places the stimulant beneath the mountain in the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Platonic love is idealised and non-physical, after Plato's theory of ideal Forms.

clue.text: Demand placed on trial witness would shame devil

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what a witness swears to do in court
second meaning: from the proverb that honesty shames the devil

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs 'tell the truth and shame the devil', so the phrase is what would shame him.
explanation.definitionFit: Witnesses swear an oath to be honest, and the old saying holds that honesty puts Satan to shame.

clue.text: It's essential to keep documents together

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a basic item or main ingredient
second meaning: a wire clip that fastens papers

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one office tip; it is two meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a basic food or commodity, and also the bent wire clip used to fasten sheets of paper.

clue.text: Simple job to acquire large land

indicators.note: acquiring something means taking it in, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: a cinch is something very easy
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

explanation.surface: An easy task to buy a big plot of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' is a verb here, as in landing a deal, not ground or property.
explanation.definitionFit: To clinch a deal or a title is to secure it, just as one lands a contract.

clue.text: Worry penalty is oddly deficient

indicators.note: lacking in the odd places means the first, third, fifth and so on are dropped

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone fretting that a punishment falls short.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat someone, as in 'what's eating you?', is to trouble or bother them.

clue.text: Psycho's hospitality business Seattle mob destroyed

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so its letters can be rebuilt differently

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A psychopath's hotel is wrecked by a gang from Seattle.
explanation.walkthrough: Psycho is Hitchcock's film, not a madman: its killer Norman Bates runs a motel.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hitchcock's film Psycho, the roadside lodging run by Norman Bates is where the shower murder happens.

clue.text: Derby location covered in sheep sometimes

indicators.note: covered in means held inside, so the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A racecourse that is sometimes overrun with sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is the famous English flat horse race, run each year at Epsom Downs in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs racecourse in Surrey hosts the Derby, England's best-known flat race.

clue.text: Fur old pet swallowed

indicators.note: whatever is swallowed ends up inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a cat is a common pet
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A furball from an elderly animal that ate something.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's coat is its covering of hair or fur.

clue.text: Are so many able to provide pets?

parts.note: if you can, you are able
oodles is a great many

explanation.surface: A question about whether a crowd of people can supply animals for a home.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'are able' then 'so many' the clue gives the pieces in answer order; 'pets' is a verb, not animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet is to kiss and cuddle amorously, and canoodling is exactly that.

clue.text: Cutting short recording is an easy goal

indicators.note: cutting short means trimming off the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: recording onto tape

explanation.surface: A footballer remarks that cutting a highlight reel short is no challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, a tap-in is a goal scored with a gentle touch from close range.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap-in is a simple close-range score needing only a light touch of the ball.

clue.text: Sailed from the centre to get royal's lunchtime schedule

indicators.note: from the centre asks for the core letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A palace aide consulting the king's or queen's daily diary for the midday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of each word is taken: two letters from the even-length words, three from lunchtime.
explanation.definitionFit: To yacht is to travel in a sailing boat for pleasure, so the past tense matches sailed.

clue.text: Computer hacker initially takes on risk for play

indicators.note: to take something on is to take it in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter
a bet is a risk taken on an outcome

explanation.surface: A hacker breaks into a computer, gambling with risk to stage a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: MAC followed by the hacker's H forms MACH, which takes the risk word inside, before the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth is Shakespeare's tragedy about a Scottish lord who murders his king.
